Repeat blood count, kidney and liver tests and blood glucose as arranged. Bone blood tests and ECG are repeated when clinically indicated. PSA, testosterone and scans follow the individual cancer plan.

If treatment is interrupted for more than 7 days, contact the team before restarting: a new loading dose is normally needed. Some interacting medicines require a different dose or separation by at least 6 hours. Do not change the dose yourself; ask pharmacy to check every new medicine.

phases.label: Pembrolizumab with continuous axitinib
notes: Pembrolizumab 200 mg is given intravenously every 21 days. Axitinib starts at 5 mg twice daily, about 12 hours apart, continuously, with or without food. Only your team may change the dose. phases.label: Enfortumab infusion days 1, 8 and 15
notes: Enfortumab vedotin is given on days 1, 8 and 15 of a 28-day cycle. The starting dose is 1.25 mg/kg, capped at 125 mg per dose. The team may hold, reduce or stop treatment for side effects. Treatment continues while appropriate according to benefit and tolerance.

Blood count, kidney/liver tests and glucose on days 1, 8 and 15 in cycle 1, then on day 1 of later cycles in the NCCP schedule, with additional tests as clinically needed. Lipase and HbA1c on day 1 if indicated. Review skin and nerve symptoms throughout; assess eye or breathing symptoms promptly.

phases.label: High-dose chemotherapy and transplant support
notes: Carboplatin AUC7 is followed by etoposide 750 mg/m² on days −5, −4 and −3. Your stored stem cells are infused on day 0. Growth-factor injections start on day +1 and continue until the team confirms neutrophil recovery. These day numbers are relative to the stem-cell infusion.

Prescribed anti-sickness treatment is needed across the high-dose days. The local transplant plan includes antiviral and antifungal prevention, mouth care, a proton-pump inhibitor and Pneumocystis pneumonia prevention. Co-trimoxazole starts only after engraftment; the team specifies the stop date. Irradiated cellular blood components are required from one week before conditioning until 12 months after stem-cell infusion.

phases.label: Five-day chemotherapy and protection plan
notes: Paclitaxel is given on day 1. Cisplatin and ifosfamide are given on days 1–5, with bladder-protecting mesna each day. Growth-factor injections start on day 6 until neutrophil recovery under local policy. Four 21-day cycles are planned, subject to consultant review.

Cisplatin needs a high-risk anti-sickness plan and prescribed hydration/electrolytes. Ifosfamide needs mesna and adequate fluids. Paclitaxel needs prescribed allergy premedication; reconcile steroid doses with antiemetics. Aprepitant may increase ifosfamide brain toxicity, so pharmacy must review the combination. Growth factor is included from day 6. Retain prescribed mouth care, pain relief and stomach protection.

phases.label: BCG instillation and home precautions
notes: BCG is placed in the bladder once weekly for six weeks. Maintenance uses three weekly instillations at months 3,6 and12 for intermediate-risk disease; high/very-high-risk plans may add months 18,24,30 and36. Your urologist confirms the course according to risk, response, tolerance and supply.

Routine anti-sickness or steroid premedication is not usually needed. The source asks for no fluids for four hours before and until two hours after instillation; confirm this is safe with your team, especially with fluid-sensitive conditions. Obtain written instructions for restarting fluids, passing urine, toilet hygiene, spill management and sexual precautions for your exact product.

phases.label: Bladder instillation and prescribed preparation
notes: Both medicines are given at each weekly induction visit for six weeks. Selected patients then receive treatment monthly for 18 months, beginning six weeks after the final induction dose. Maintenance depends on response and tolerability; it is not automatic.

The source includes prescribed sodium bicarbonate1200 mg the night before and1200 mg one hour before treatment to reduce bladder irritation. Anti-sickness medicine may be considered if nausea followed a previous instillation. Pain or spasm medicines are individual prescriptions; ask before taking ibuprofen or other medicines.
